title: Mildred K NDE 3808
content: I got off work that morning, feeling like death warmed over. My boss drove me to my doctor's office. I saw my doctor coming toward me - I collapsed. Next thing I knew it was the next morning and my doctor was having me loaded into an ambulance. He told me that our hospital was a small community one and didn't have enough oxygen to keep me alive. The ambulance was en-route to St. Francis Hospital and I was not getting enough oxygen to keep breathing. That's when the emergency medical technician asked the driver what our estimated time of arrival was because he was running out of oxygen. I wanted to cry, but I remembered that my family did not know what had happened to me - and then it happened! Everything was totally black for a minute or so. Then I found myself in the most vibrantly beautiful rose garden that anyone could ever imagine! The foliage was vibrant, glossy green and the rose blossoms were absolutely enormous and so exquisite in both color and fragrance. I was very peaceful in my own mind, not really thinking of anything except the overwhelming peace and glorious beauty of the beautiful, seemingly endless garden of perfection. I was there surrounded by perfection. Then, I heard a noise behind me, a slight rustling. Then I saw my mother, who has been deceased since 1990. There were others with her; my father, deceased in 1960; my sister, deceased in 1980. Others of my family were standing behind mom, dad, and sis. I asked mom if she loved it here, because I sure did. Mom had a rather worried look on her face. I asked mom what was wrong. She said that I had to leave this place because I was not to be here yet! I told her that I never wanted to leave this wonderful place! She told me that I had to return, it was not my time yet. I told her that I didn't want to leave and she told me that I had to, it wasn't my time. A few minutes later, everything went black and I woke up from a coma nine days later. The doctor said that I was dead on arrival. They revived me three times that first night and called my family in because I wasn't going to survive that first night. I woke out of a coma nine days later surrounded by my crying daughters and family.

environment.environment_other_detail: A "vibrantly beautiful rose garden" with "vibrant, glossy green" foliage and "enormous" rose blossoms with exquisite "color and fragrance," described as a "seemingly endless garden of perfection."

boundary_and_return.return_method_other_detail: After being told to leave, "A few minutes later, everything went black and I woke up from a coma nine days later."

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Collapsed at doctor's office; later in ambulance with inadequate oxygen and described going black; later physician said she was "dead on arrival" and revived three times.

stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: Blackness first, then arrival in a garden; encounter with deceased relatives; told she must leave; then blackness and awakening later from coma.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: The initial transitional phase is described as "totally black for a minute or so" rather than a tunnel with light; environment specifically a rose garden with strong emphasis on fragrance and enormous blossoms.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: "Everything was totally black for a minute or so. Then I found myself in the most vibrantly beautiful rose garden that anyone could ever imagine!"; "I had to leave this place because I was not to be here yet!"; "The doctor said that I was dead on arrival. They revived me three times that first night."
